Foreword by His Excellency the Right Honourable
Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Eswatini
For over forty years, the partnership between
the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini and
the United Nations has stood as a cornerstone
of our nation’s development journey. Through
this enduring collaboration, we have made
significant progress in advancing human
development, strengthening institutions, and
improving the quality of life for our people.
As we open a new chapter in our shared
development story, we must acknowledge that
doing the same things and expecting different
results will not deliver the transformation we
seek. The challenges of todays - economic
diversification, youth unemployment, climate
change, and widening global inequalities
demand a bold shift in mindset and a renewed
determination to act differently. This is the
moment for a national drive for transformation,
calling on all of us Government, the United
Nations, Development Partners, the Private
Sector, Civil Society, and every LiSwati to work
together with urgency, unity, and purpose.
The CF 2026–2030 is a collective commitment
to transformation. Aligned with His Majesty
King Mswati III’s Nkwe Vision and anchored
in Eswatini’s National Development Plan
(NDP) 2023/24-2027/28 and Government’s
Programme of Action 2024-2029, it offers
a shared roadmap towards inclusive and
sustainable development. It is a call to innovate,
to collaborate, and to build a resilient Eswatini
that truly leaves no one behind.
Wearemindfulthatnonationhaseverdeveloped
through aid or external effort alone. Sustainable
progress must be homegrown, nationally
owned, and people-centred, driven by creativity,
resilience, and enterprise of its people. The
Government will continue to lead and provide
policy direction, while working closely with the
United Nations to ensure that international
support strengthens national capacities and
sustains our collective gains for generations to
come.
As we embark on the“last mile”toward achieving
the 2030 Agenda, we will keep our goals
ambitious enough to inspire transformation, yet
realistic enough to deliver measurable results
by creating jobs, strengthening public services,
advancing gender equality, empowering youth,
and protecting our environment. The UN’s
technical expertise, global experience, and
convening power will remain vital as Eswatini
navigates an evolving global landscape.
The Government of Eswatini reaffirms its
unwavering commitment to walk hand in hand
with the United Nations system in driving the
country’s development and transformation
agenda for the prosperity of every Liswati and
the generations to come.
His Excellency the Right Honourable
Russell Mmiso Dlamini
Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Eswatini

Foreword by the Minister of Economic
Planning and Development
TheCF2026–2030marksanimportantmilestone
in Eswatini’s development cooperation with
the United Nations Development System. It
reflects the enduring partnership between
the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini
and the United Nations, as well as our shared
determination to accelerate progress towards
inclusive and sustainable development for all
emaSwati.
This CF has been developed through a
collaborative and consultative process that
brought together government institutions, the
private sector, civil society, academia, and
development partners. It is firmly aligned with
Hon. Dr. Thambo Gina
Minister of Economic Planning and
Development
Kingdom of Eswatini
Eswatini’s National Development Plan (NDP)
2023/24–2027/28, which seeks to transform
the country into a high-income, resilient,
and inclusive economy, while advancing the
aspirations of the African Union’s Agenda
2063 and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable
Development.
The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini
welcomes theCF2026–2030asakey instrument
for guiding and coordinating United Nations
support in the country. It provides a coherent
framework through which the UN system and
its agencies will continue to complement
national efforts in critical areas such as human
capital development, economic diversification,
environmental sustainability, and institutional
strengthening. The CF emphasis on inclusive
social well-being and shared and sustainable
prosperity resonates deeply with our national
priorities of improving livelihoods, reducing
poverty, and ensuring that no one is left behind.
On behalf of the Government of the Kingdom
of Eswatini, I wish to extend our sincere
appreciationtotheUnitedNations,development
partners, and all stakeholders who contributed
to the development of this CF. We look forward
to continued collaboration in translating its
commitments into tangible results that improve
the lives of all citizens and strengthen Eswatini’s
pathway to sustainable growth and prosperity.
Hon. Dr. Thambo Gina
Minister of Economic Planning andDevelopment
Kingdom of EswatiniV
Foreword by the UN Resident
Coordinator in the Kingdom of Eswatini
The CF 2026–2030 represents a renewed and
deliberate partnership between the United
Nations and the Government of the Kingdom
of Eswatini. It comes at a time when the
country faces both complex challenges and
transformative opportunities. The Framework
reflects our collective resolve to translate
ambitionintoaction,tomovebeyondaspirational
planning toward practical, evidence-based
solutions that improve lives and drive inclusive,
sustainable growth.
This CF is not a “plug and play” document. It is
the outcome of a thoughtful, nationally owned
George Wachira
United Nations Resident
Coordinator
Kingdom of Eswatini
process that applied strategic foresight and
systems thinking to anticipate risks, identify
emerging opportunities, and chart adaptive
responses to Eswatini’s development realities.
Through extensive consultations across all
sectors, the CF integrates perspectives from
government, civil society, the private sector,
academia, and vulnerable groups to ensure that
every voice informs the country’s transformation
pathway.
Anchored in Eswatini’s National Development
Plan (NDP) 2023/24–2027/28, the African
Union’s Agenda 2063, and the 2030 Agenda for
Sustainable Development, the CF focuses on
two (2) mutually reinforcing priorities: Inclusive
Social Well-Being and Shared and Sustainable
Prosperity. These priorities directly address the
country’smostpressingneeds,includingtackling
high unemployment and inequality, accelerating
economic diversification, enhancing service
delivery, and building resilience to climate and
fiscal shocks.
This CF is designed for implementation. It
provides a clear results structure, identifies
catalytic interventions, and embeds
accountability mechanisms to ensure that
commitments translate into measurable
progress. It recognises that sustainable
development requires coherence between
policy, investment, and institutional capacity,
and that foresight, innovation, and evidence
must underpin decision-making at every level.
The United Nations Country Team stands
ready to accompany Eswatini on this journey,
not merely as a development partner, but
as a convener, an enabler, and a co-creator
of practical solutions. Through this CF, we
reaffirm our shared commitment to advancing
a prosperous, inclusive, and resilient Eswatini
where no one is left behind and where national
development is both visionary and grounded in
real-world impact.
George Wachira
United Nations Resident Coordinator
Kingdom of EswatiniJoint Statement of the United Nations
Country Team in Eswatini
In its resolution 72/279 of 31 May 2018, the United Nations General Assembly established a dedicated,
impartial, independent, empowered, and sustainable development-focused coordination function
for the United Nations Development System (UNDS). The United Nations Sustainable Development
Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), also referred to as theCF is the primary instrument for planning and
implementing UN development activities at the country level for the period 2026-2030 in partnership
with the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini. It represents the collective commitment of the UNDS
to support national priorities and the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
The CF 2026–2030 articulates the UN’s collective response to support Eswatini in realizing its vision
of becoming a high-income country by 2050 through sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth. It
emphasizes promoting access to quality social services, strengthening systems and institutional
capacities, and leveraging the UN’s comparative advantages to respond to the multidimensional
challenges posed by climate change, energy, youth unemployment, inequality among others. Aligned
with Eswatini’s national priorities, the CF is guided by the principles of leaving no one behind, human
rights, gender equality, resilience building, and sustainability. It brings together all UN entities: resident
and non-resident, to deliver as one and to leverage their comparative advantages and global expertise
for greater coherence, synergy, and collective impact.
This Joint Statement reflects the shared vision and commitment of the United Nations Country Team
(UNCT) in Eswatini to implement the CF in partnership with the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini,
development partners, civil society, academia, the private sector, and communities.
It is a collective pledge by all the signatory UN agencies: resident and non-resident, operating in the
country to jointly deliver as one under the leadership of the Resident Coordinator. It demonstrates that
the UNCT stands united behind shared strategic priorities, a single results framework, and common
accountability to the Government and people of Eswatini. It is the UNCTs commitment to formalize
how it will work through joint planning, joint implementation, and joint monitoring, to ensure alignment
with the Management and Accountability Framework (MAF) as the formal structure to reinforce roles,
responsibilities and performance to ensure accountability through results and reporting across UN
Country Teams. Finally, it serves as a mutual commitment between the UN and the Government (and
by extension, the people of Eswatini) and reassures national authorities that all UN agencies, regardless
of their presence or size, are aligned with national priorities, the National Development Plan (NDP
2023/24-2027/28), Southern African Development Community (SADC) Vision 2050, and African Union
(AU) Agenda 2063.
During the period 2026–2030, 21 UN agencies and entities have committed to the implementation of
the CF in Eswatini. These are:
1. Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
2. International Organization for Migration (IOM)
3. Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
4. United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF)
5. United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
6. United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
7. World Food Programme (WFP)
8. World Health Organization (WHO)
9. International Labour Organization (ILO)
10. International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
11. International Trade Centre (ITC)
12. International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
VI13. Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)
14. United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA)
15. United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
16. United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat)
17. United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)
18. United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
19. United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
20. United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women)
21. United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)
Together, these agencies combine resident operational presence with the technical and normative
strengths of non-resident entities to provide coordinated, efficient, and impactful support to national
development priorities.
Recognizing the limitedin-countrypresenceof someUNentitiesaspartoftheongoingUN80reforms,and
the associated evolving global and regional development architecture, the UN in Eswatini will leverage
regional collaborative platforms and country-to-country capacity transfer approaches to supplement
national capacities for the effective delivery of the CF. This will include drawing on the expertise of the
regional economic commission, subregional hubs, and technical clusters based in various countries.
Such collaboration will ensure that Eswatini benefits from specialized policy advice, analytical tools,
and surge technical back-up across all output areas of the CF. Through these mechanisms, the UN in
Eswatini will strengthen coherence, enhance joint programming, and ensure that the CF is implemented
efficiently and inclusively in partnership with the following partnering Government Ministries:
1. Prime Minister’s Office
2. Deputy Prime Minister’s Office
3. Ministry of Natural Resources and Energy
4. Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs
5. Ministry of Home Affairs
6. Ministry of Public Works and Transport
7. Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
8. Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology
9. Ministry of Housing and Urban Development
10. Ministry of Sports, Culture and Youth Affairs
11. Ministry of Tourism and Environmental Affairs
12. Ministry of Public Service
13. Ministry of Agriculture
14. Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Trade
15. Ministry of Health
16. Ministry of Finance
17. Ministry of Education and Training
18. Ministry of Labor and Social Security
19. Ministry of Tinkhundla Administration and Development
20. Ministry of Economic Planning and Development
21. Ministry of Defence and National Security
Through appending their signatures below, representatives of the UN agencies, entities and Cabinet in
Eswatini reaffirm their commitment to working coherently and effectively, and to leverage their comparative advantage, to accompany the Government and people of Eswatini in building a resilient, inclusive,
and prosperous society, leaving no one behind.
